title: Flexbox in React Native
tagline: Which property goes on the container, which on the child, and which axis it moves.
intro: React Native lays everything out with flexbox, like the web, with one difference that trips everyone: flexDirection defaults to column, not row.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: Pick the axis first; every other property is relative to it.

blocks.caption: The order to think in when a layout looks wrong.

items.label: flexDirection
items.detail: Sets the main axis: column stacks children downwards, row lays them side by side
explain: Values are column (the default), row, column-reverse and row-reverse. The other axis, at right angles, is the cross axis.
Everything below is phrased as main or cross axis, so changing this one property rotates what they all do.

items.label: justifyContent
items.detail: Spreads children along the main axis: start, end, centre or with space between
explain: Values: flex-start, flex-end, center, space-between, space-around, space-evenly.
space-between puts the first and last child on the edges; space-evenly makes every gap, edges included, the same size.

items.label: alignItems
items.detail: Places children across the cross axis; stretch fills it unless a size is set
explain: Values: stretch (the default), flex-start, flex-end, center, baseline.
A child with a fixed width in a column container ignores stretch, which is why one card is narrower than the rest.

items.label: alignSelf
items.detail: Overrides alignItems for one child, set on that child rather than the container
explain: Same values as alignItems. Use it for the one badge that should hug the right while its siblings stretch.
It is the only property here that lives on the child; the rest describe how a container arranges its children.

items.label: flexWrap + alignContent
items.detail: Wrap breaks children into several lines; alignContent spreads those lines across the cross axis
explain: Example: a column container with maxHeight 200 and ten children that do not fit. flexWrap: 'wrap' starts a second column.
alignContent then decides where those two columns sit. With a single line it does nothing, which is why it often seems broken.

rows: flex-start, flex-end, center, space-between, space-around, space-evenly

blocks.caption: row makes justifyContent horizontal and alignItems vertical

body: direction (ltr or rtl) flips start and end for right-to-left languages; it does not change the axis.
